paper_metadata.title: Extract, Define, Canonicalize: An LLM-based Framework for Knowledge Graph Construction
paper_metadata.venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP 2024), pages 9820–9836
paper_metadata.abstract: The paper proposes Extract-Define-Canonicalize (EDC), an LLM-based three-phase framework for knowledge graph construction from text. It performs open triplet extraction, generates definitions for induced schema components, and canonicalizes them against either a target schema or a self-generated schema; an optional trained schema retriever supports iterative refinement. The authors evaluate it on three KGC benchmarks and report high-quality triplet extraction without parameter tuning of the base LLM.

problem_addressed: Automated knowledge graph construction from natural-language text, focused on relational triplet extraction and canonicalization. Existing prompt-based LLM KGC methods require target-schema information in the prompt, which does not scale to large schemas and is unsuitable when no fixed schema exists; open extraction also leaves redundant and ambiguous relation phrases.

methodology.primary_family: Zero-shot and few-shot LLM prompting (without task-specific base-model training)
secondary_families: Instruction-tuned or fine-tuned LLM methods (trained schema-retriever component)
methodology.description: EDC executes in order: (1) an LLM uses few-shot open information extraction to emit [subject, relation, object] triples without including a schema; (2) the LLM writes contextual natural-language definitions for extracted relation/schema components; (3) a sentence-transformer similarity search retrieves candidate relation components and the LLM verifies whether a proposed replacement is semantically valid. With a supplied target schema, non-alignable components and their triples are excluded; without one, non-alignable components are added to an initially empty canonical schema. Optional EDC+R performs another extraction pass using a hint containing prior extracted entities/relations plus top retrieved schema relations. Its fine-tuned E5-Mistral schema retriever maps text and defined relations into a relevance-oriented vector space. Contributions detailed: EDC supports both large predefined schemas and schema induction; the trained Schema Retriever improves refinement; experiments compare EDC/EDC+R against trained and canonicalization baselines across target-alignment and self-canonicalization settings.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: Schema is central and may be either externally supplied or induced. EDC defines each extracted relation in natural language, embeds definitions, retrieves nearest candidate schema components, and asks the LLM to validate replacement. In target alignment, triples must conform to the target schema and rejected mappings are excluded. In self-canonicalization, the system begins with an empty canonical schema and adds components when no valid equivalent exists; this is schema canonicalization, not ontology discovery in the formal ontology-engineering sense.

text_to_kg_stages: Entity and concept extraction (entities in subject/object triple positions; optional candidate-entity extraction)
Ontology or schema discovery (self-generated canonical relation schema)
Graph construction (open and canonicalized triplet KG)
Graph validation and correction (LLM verification of candidate schema substitutions; refinement)

input_output.input_type: Unstructured natural-language text, with an optional predefined relation schema for target alignment; EDC+R additionally uses previously extracted triples and retrieved relation definitions as prompting hints.
input_output.input_granularity: Individual text instances/sentences paired with triples in the benchmark test sets; the paper reports average extracted triples per sentence. The framework is also described as composable with sentence-level chunking for documents exceeding LLM context windows.
input_output.output_representation: Lists of relational triples [Subject, Relation, Object], first forming an open KG and then a canonicalized KG. In target alignment, relation labels are aligned to a supplied schema; in self-canonicalization, a concise induced canonical relation schema is produced.

datasets: WebNLG+2020 v3.0 semantic-parsing test split: 1,165 text–triple pairs; 159 unique relation types
REBEL original test partition: random sample of 1,000 text–triple pairs from 105,516 entries; 200 relation types
Wiki-NRE test split: sample of 1,000 text–triple pairs from 29,619 entries; 45 relation types
Novel fictional dataset: 50 annotated entries using the Wiki-NRE schema, created to test possible LLM benchmark contamination
Additional comparative datasets in appendix: CoNLL04 and SciERC; Re-DOCRED combined with LingMess and sentence chunking

metrics: Automatic token-based triple Precision, Recall, and F1 using the WEBNLG evaluation script
Partial match: at least a partial triple match, disregarding element type
Strict match: exact triplet match including element types
Exact match: complete triple match, disregarding element type
Number of relation types as schema conciseness (lower is better)
Redundancy score: average cosine similarity of each canonical relation to its nearest counterpart (lower is better)
Inter-annotator agreement of 0.94 for two independent annotators
Schema Retriever Recall@10: WebNLG 0.823, REBEL 0.663, Wiki-NRE 0.818
baselines: REGEN (T5 sequence-to-sequence with reinforcement learning) on WebNLG
GenIE (BART sequence-to-sequence constrained generation) on REBEL and Wiki-NRE
Open KG: initial OIE output, for self-canonicalization
CESI: clustering-based open-KG canonicalization, applied to the Open KG
ChatIE and CodeKGC in appendix comparisons on CoNLL04, SciERC, and Wiki-NRE
GenIE on the novel fictional dataset
EDC+R without Schema Retriever and EDC+R-lastround ablations
evaluation.setting: Two principal settings. Target Alignment evaluates recovery of reference triples conforming to a provided relation schema on WebNLG, sampled REBEL, and sampled Wiki-NRE; EDC and one-refinement EDC+R are evaluated with GPT-4, GPT-3.5, or Mistral-7b as OIE LLMs. Self Canonicalization provides no target schema, uses GPT-3.5 for OIE, compares EDC with its Open-KG output and CESI, and uses targeted blinded human assessment by two annotators. Appendix tests more refinement, ablations, a 50-item fictional dataset, small-schema comparisons, and a Re-DOCRED integration experiment.

value: Author-reported: avoids putting a large full schema into the initial extraction prompt; supports both target-schema alignment and self-canonicalization when no fixed schema is available.
Author-reported/experimental: contextual LLM-generated definitions plus LLM verification aim to avoid the over-generalization of embedding-only or clustering canonicalization.
Experimental: one refinement with a trained Schema Retriever consistently improved target-alignment results in the reported ablation.

Review-level inference: separating schema definition and canonicalization from initial open extraction makes the approach modular and enables an auditable execution order, although the paper does not test a formal auditability measure.

value: Author-reported: EDC requires many LLM calls and is costly; using GPT-3.5-turbo for all components cost about USD 0.009 per example.
Author-reported: the study only canonicalizes schema components/relations and does not provide a general entity de-duplication mechanism.

Experimental/evaluation caveat: REBEL and Wiki-NRE reference triples can be incomplete or include information not directly stated in text, so automatic reference-based scores can penalize valid extractions; this restricts interpretation of reported scores.

Review-level inference: output correctness still relies on prompted LLM extraction and LLM mapping decisions; vector retrieval can return irrelevant relations, so the method does not itself guarantee factuality or prevent hallucination.
Experimental: EDC alone was not always superior on small-schema CoNLL04 and SciERC; the gains over prior LLM approaches there required refinement.
